# SceneStrip

> SceneStrip is a paid macOS app (one-time purchase) that lists the local videos in your folders with 10 evenly spaced thumbnails per file, so you can see what is inside a video before you press play. It reads folders in place, does not import or upload anything, and runs entirely on the Mac.

Developer: Shinichi Nomura (indie developer, Japan). Distributed only through the Mac App Store.

## What it does

- Register up to 10 folders (local or external drives). SceneStrip scans them and shows every video with 10 thumbnails taken at equal intervals across its length.
- Thumbnails and metadata are cached, so reopening a folder is instant. Refresh rescans only files that were added, changed or removed.
- Shows file name, path, size, modified date, duration and resolution for each video.
- Favorites, Finder tags (read-only) and SceneStrip's own tags, with filtering by any of them.
- Sort by capture date, file name or recently played.
- Built-in player with per-video bookmarks. Can be switched to open videos in the default macOS player instead.
- Rename and move-to-Trash from inside the app.
- Favorites and custom tags are stored in a small sidecar file inside the managed folder, so they travel with an external drive to another Mac.

## What it does not do

- No video editing, exporting or cloud sync.
- No library import: files stay where they are.
- No account, no upload, no tracking. All processing happens on the Mac.

## Requirements and formats

- macOS 14.0 or later.
- Formats: mp4, mov, m4v, avi, mkv. avi and mkv are supported on Apple Silicon Macs only.

## Price

- One-time purchase on the Mac App Store. JPY 150 in Japan, USD 0.99 in the US (other storefronts vary).

## Typical questions this app answers

- How can I see what is inside many video files on a Mac without opening each one?
- Is there a Mac app that shows multiple thumbnails per video, like a contact sheet, for a whole folder?
- How do I organize GoPro, drone or iPhone videos on an external SSD with tags and favorites, without importing them into Photos?
